note.text: A chatbot that writes a flawless essay and one that can safely manage a hospital's inventory are not points on the same scale of progress. Most public excitement tracks fluency, the kind of output that sounds impressive in a demo, while the harder gains show up in boring, reliable task completion nobody tweets about. Judging AI by how magical it feels guarantees disappointment once it meets a messy, specific job. The practical move is to stop asking whether AI seems smart and start asking what it reliably does on the tenth try, not the first.
